title: Ethiopian Tomato Chilli Sauce
community: All of Ethiopia — the fresh tomato-chilli table sauce
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Silsi — a smooth, slightly spiced tomato sauce made from fresh tomatoes, onion, garlic, green chilli, and a touch of berbere. The Ethiopian table sauce served alongside tibs, grilled fish, and grilled meats — lighter and fresher than awaze.
longDesc: Silsi is Ethiopia's fresh tomato table sauce — lighter than awaze, brighter than berbere-based condiments, and providing a fresh acid note alongside richer preparations. It appears on every restaurant table alongside tibs and grilled preparations.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion and garlic until golden — 5 minutes.
Add green chillies and berbere. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes until completely soft.
Blend with lemon juice and coriander until smooth.
Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.
chefTips: Silsi should be smooth — blend thoroughly.
The green chilli (not berbere) provides the primary heat here.
The berbere is a background note only — just ½ tsp.
Add lemon after blending — preserves the bright colour.
commonMistakes: Too much berbere — overpowers the fresh tomato character.
cookingScience: Cooking the tomatoes before blending concentrates the lycopene and breaks down the pectin in the cell walls — producing a smoother texture than raw tomato blending and concentrating the umami compounds (glutamate) released during cooking.
sustainabilityTips: Fresh seasonal tomatoes — peak nutrition and flavour.
servedWith: As a dipping sauce with injera
culturalNote: Silsi is the light condiment of the Ethiopian table — where awaze is intense and kibbeh is rich, silsi is bright and fresh. It provides the tomato-forward note that balances the heavy spice and fat of the great wats.
